The entity name and EIN are required for every subsequent registration and permit.

items.original_text: Filing step: Register for the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector and file the Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk. What to say: Register online at sftreasurer.org using the entity name and EIN; the Business Account Number (BAN) is issued within 1–5 days. The fee is tiered by projected gross receipts (e.g., $55 for under $100k, $95 for under $250k). File the FBN statement in person or by mail with photo ID, then publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Every city permit application asks for the BAN.

items.original_text: Filing step: Engage an ABC license broker to locate and escrow an available Type 42 license from a bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD, and begin the license purchase negotiation in parallel with the CUA application preparation. What to say: Tell the broker the license must be transferred from a bar (Type 42 or 48) currently located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District boundaries (roughly 16th to Cesar Chavez, Mission to Potrero). Ask for a purchase price, escrow timeline and any known issues (protests, ABC holds, unpaid taxes). Budget 90–180 days for the transfer plus 1–3 months if a PCN finding is required. Do not close escrow until the CUA is approved, but secure an option or agreement contingent on CUA approval.

items.original_text: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including a good-neighbor operating plan, a letter of intent to transfer an ABC Type 42 license from within the SUD, and a draft security plan per § 202.2. What to say: Submit the CUA application through the Planning portal with the BAN, a project narrative describing the wine bar concept, the closing hour (1 a.m.), the limited kitchen menu, live entertainment (genre, days, end time), and the commitment to transfer a Type 42 license from within the SUD. Include a good-neighbor plan with a security protocol, neighborhood liaison contact, and a statement that the bar will comply with § 249.60 lighting and signage limits. Request a pre-filing community meeting per § 312 if required. The application fee is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 $2,747 base) and may qualify for First Year Free fee waivers if the business is new.

items.original_text: Filing step: Commission an acoustic report and soundproofing plan for live entertainment, and submit it as a supplemental document to Planning and in anticipation of the Entertainment Commission POE application. What to say: Hire an acoustic engineer to measure existing sound transmission to adjacent and upstairs residential units and design soundproofing (insulation, resilient channels, double-glazed windows, door seals). The report should specify maximum sound levels at the property line (typically 55–60 dBA) and recommend mitigation. Submit the report to Planning with a cover letter committing to implement the recommendations before opening. The Entertainment Commission will ask for it at the POE hearing.

items.original_text: Filing step: After the CUA is approved and the appeal period has run (30 days), close escrow on the ABC Type 42 license transfer and file the ABC transfer application with proof of the CUA approval, a signed lease, a seller's permit, and a request for a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the Board of… What to say: Submit the ABC person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer application at abc.ca.gov with the CUA motion, the signed lease, the entity formation documents, the seller's permit (obtained from CDTFA), and the $1,000–$1,600 license fee. Planning's zoning sign-off and the PCN finding can add 1–3 months to ABC's standard 60-day timeline.

items.original_text: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application for the limited kitchen and bar, and the building permit application to DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, both routed to Planning, Fire, PUC and DPH. What to say: Through the DPH portal submit two sets of scaled kitchen and bar drawings, interior/exterior photos, a menu describing the limited cooking (small plates, charcuterie, panini), and an equipment list (panini press, refrigeration, three-compartment sink, hand sinks). Pay the plan-check fee ($828–$2,207 depending on review hours). In parallel, file the building permit application through PermitSF with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the bar area, the limited kitchen, the entertainment space, ADA upgrades, and any structural or MEP work. The permit will be routed to Planning (for CUA conformance), DPH (for health plan check), Fire (for occupancy and hood suppression) and PUC (for FOG interceptor). Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% construction completion.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 270 to 660 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $25,000. Notes: The timeline spans 9–22 months and is driven by the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to hearing plus 30-day appeal period), the ABC Type 42 license transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD (90–180 days, extended to 120–270 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to undue concentration), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days including posting and hearing). The building permit with change of use adds 14–120 days for plan review. The cost range covers city fees only: CUA application (~$3,100, CPI-adjusted), POE application ($2,708), ABC license transfer application fee ($1,000–$1,600, not including the purchase price of the license from the selling bar, which is a private transaction often costing $20k–$100k+ in saturated markets), DPH plan check ($828–$2,207), Health Permit to Operate application ($470), building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), and business registration ($55–$700 depending on gross receipts). The license purchase price, construction costs, architect and acoustic engineer fees, broker fees, and insurance premiums are not government fees and are not included in this range. The critical path is: (1) identify and escrow an available Type 42 license from a bar within the SUD (2–4 months), (2) file and win the CUA (4–10 months), (3) close the license transfer and obtain the PCN finding (3–9 months, overlapping with construction), (4) obtain the POE permit (2–4 months, after CUA approval), (5) complete tenant improvements and pass final inspections (2–4 months). Start the license search and the CUA application in parallel immediately after the pre-application meeting with Planning. The total timeline assumes no appeals, no CUA continuances, and that an available Type 42 license from within the SUD can be located and escrowed; if no license is available or if the seller withdraws, the project cannot proceed under current SUD rules.

items.original_text: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including a good-neighbor operating plan, a letter of intent to transfer an ABC Type 42 license from within the SUD, and a draft security plan per § 202.2. What to say: Submit the CUA application through the Planning portal with the BAN, a project narrative describing the wine bar concept, the closing hour (1 a.m.), the limited kitchen menu, live entertainment (genre, days, end time), and the commitment to transfer a Type 42 license from within the SUD. Include a good-neighbor plan with a security protocol, neighborhood liaison contact, and a statement that the bar will comply with § 249.60 lighting and signage limits. Request a pre-filing community meeting per § 312 if required. The application fee is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 $2,747 base) and may qualify for First Year Free fee waivers if the business is new.

items.original_text: Filing step: Commission an acoustic report and soundproofing plan for live entertainment, and submit it as a supplemental document to Planning and in anticipation of the Entertainment Commission POE application. What to say: Hire an acoustic engineer to measure existing sound transmission to adjacent and upstairs residential units and design soundproofing (insulation, resilient channels, double-glazed windows, door seals). The report should specify maximum sound levels at the property line (typically 55–60 dBA) and recommend mitigation. Submit the report to Planning with a cover letter committing to implement the recommendations before opening. The Entertainment Commission will ask for it at the POE hearing.

Given the undue-concentration density (51 on-sale licenses within 1,000 ft), expect ABC to require a PCN finding; coordinate with the Board of Supervisors (via the Clerk) to place the PCN resolution on the agenda. Planning's zoning sign-off and the PCN finding can add 1–3 months to ABC's standard 60-day timeline.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an EIN from the IRS. What to say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov. The entity name and EIN are required for every subsequent registration and permit.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector and file the Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk. What to say: Register online at sftreasurer.org using the entity name and EIN; the Business Account Number (BAN) is issued within 1–5 days. The fee is tiered by projected gross receipts (e.g., $55 for under $100k, $95 for under $250k). File the FBN statement in person or by mail with photo ID, then publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Every city permit application asks for the BAN.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Engage an ABC license broker to locate and escrow an available Type 42 license from a bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD, and begin the license purchase negotiation in parallel with the CUA application preparation. What to say: Tell the broker the license must be transferred from a bar (Type 42 or 48) currently located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District boundaries (roughly 16th to Cesar Chavez, Mission to Potrero). Do not close escrow until the CUA is approved, but secure an option or agreement contingent on CUA approval.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including a good-neighbor operating plan, a letter of intent to transfer an ABC Type 42 license from within the SUD, and a draft security plan per § 202.2. What to say: Submit the CUA application through the Planning portal with the BAN, a project narrative describing the wine bar concept, the closing hour (1 a.m.), the limited kitchen menu, live entertainment (genre, days, end time), and the commitment to transfer a Type 42 license from within the SUD. Include a good-neighbor plan with a security protocol, neighborhood liaison contact, and a statement that the bar will comply with § 249.60 lighting and signage limits. Request a pre-filing community meeting per § 312 if required. The application fee is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 $2,747 base) and may qualify for First Year Free fee waivers if the business is new.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Commission an acoustic report and soundproofing plan for live entertainment, and submit it as a supplemental document to Planning and in anticipation of the Entertainment Commission POE application. What to say: Hire an acoustic engineer to measure existing sound transmission to adjacent and upstairs residential units and design soundproofing (insulation, resilient channels, double-glazed windows, door seals). The report should specify maximum sound levels at the property line (typically 55–60 dBA) and recommend mitigation. Submit the report to Planning with a cover letter committing to implement the recommendations before opening. The Entertainment Commission will ask for it at the POE hearing.

After approval, the CUA motion will impose conditions; the 30-day appeal period runs from the date of the written motion.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application for the limited kitchen and bar, and the building permit application to DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, both routed to Planning, Fire, PUC and DPH. What to say: Through the DPH portal submit two sets of scaled kitchen and bar drawings, interior/exterior photos, a menu describing the limited cooking (small plates, charcuterie, panini), and an equipment list (panini press, refrigeration, three-compartment sink, hand sinks). Pay the plan-check fee ($828–$2,207 depending on review hours). In parallel, file the building permit application through PermitSF with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the bar area, the limited kitchen, the entertainment space, ADA upgrades, and any structural or MEP work. The permit will be routed to Planning (for CUA conformance), DPH (for health plan check), Fire (for occupancy and hood suppression) and PUC (for FOG interceptor). Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% construction completion.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 270 to 660 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $25,000. Notes: The timeline spans 9–22 months and is driven by the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to hearing plus 30-day appeal period), the ABC Type 42 license transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD (90–180 days, extended to 120–270 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to undue concentration), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days including posting and hearing). The building permit with change of use adds 14–120 days for plan review. The cost range covers city fees only: CUA application (~$3,100, CPI-adjusted), POE application ($2,708), ABC license transfer application fee ($1,000–$1,600, not including the purchase price of the license from the selling bar, which is a private transaction often costing $20k–$100k+ in saturated markets), DPH plan check ($828–$2,207), Health Permit to Operate application ($470), building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), and business registration ($55–$700 depending on gross receipts). The license purchase price, construction costs, architect and acoustic engineer fees, broker fees, and insurance premiums are not government fees and are not included in this range. The critical path is: (1) identify and escrow an available Type 42 license from a bar within the SUD (2–4 months), (2) file and win the CUA (4–10 months), (3) close the license transfer and obtain the PCN finding (3–9 months, overlapping with construction), (4) obtain the POE permit (2–4 months, after CUA approval), (5) complete tenant improvements and pass final inspections (2–4 months). Start the license search and the CUA application in parallel immediately after the pre-application meeting with Planning. The total timeline assumes no appeals, no CUA continuances, and that an available Type 42 license from within the SUD can be located and escrowed; if no license is available or if the seller withdraws, the project cannot proceed under current SUD rules.
